newsitem.title: FRANCE: Trichet-BoF unshakeably committed to stable franc.
newsitem.headline: Trichet-BoF unshakeably committed to stable franc.

text.p: Bank of France governor Jean-Claude Trichet said on Friday that the central bank was unshakeably committed to the stability of the franc against the most credible currencies in the European Exchange Rate Mechanism.
Nothing would justify a depreciation of the franc against these currencies, he said in a written statement.

He also said that the nine-member policy council had only one voice. "It is that of its president, governor and spokesman, as is the case in other major independent central banks in the world," he said.

Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan and Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer gave the position of the U.S. and German central banks just has he gave the position of the Bank of France, Trichet said.

"In Paris, as in Frankfurt, as in Washington, the members of the council speak in a personal capacity. They clearly have the right to do so within the limits of our independent status, given our appreciation of the overriding interest which the law requires of us which is to defend monetary stability," he said.
Three members of the council made public statements this week on monetary policy, of which two of them questioned the bank's cautious approach on interest rates.
